label: s3_rtxpro6000_small_mtp
note: Stage 2 on the cheapest NVIDIA card that came close (s1_rtxpro6000_nvfp4_fi: SLO miss at break-even 1.03 req/s, 0.79 req/s done). Two levers, one box: (1) host right-sized from 8 vCPU/32 GiB to 4 vCPU/16 GiB; measured on a live PRO 6000 box mid-run, anon memory was 4.6 GB (the rest of the 32 GB peak was reclaimable weight page cache) and CPU averaged ~1.4 cores. $/h 2.88 -> 2.42, so break-even 1.03 -> 0.86 req/s. p6_small_base re-measures s1's flags on the small host (CPU starvation would show as TTFT). (2) MTP with Google's assistant head (OpenRelay's recipe uses MTP 2 on MI355X): at ~0.8 req/s the box carries ~50 running requests at ~10K context, so each decode step re-reads a lot of KV; MTP cuts the number of decode steps per output token. Text client at 0.86 req/s gives MTP acceptance on real text (random tokens overstate it). Rates are absolute req/s; 120 s screen, seed 7.

servers.name: p6_small_base
servers.launch: vllm serve /root/models/nvfp4 --served-model-name gemma --port 8000 --language-model-only --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --async-scheduling --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prompt-tokens-details --reasoning-parser gemma4 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 --max-model-len 32768 --attention-backend FLASHINFER
